**Block H — real site icon and preview image.**
> 1. Look at the **icons** on the left of items. For real sites (MDN, GitHub, Figma, Wikipedia, Hacker News), the app now **tries to load the actual site icon**; if it loads, you'll see the real favicon, and if the network can't reach it, it **falls back** to the coloured letter tile automatically. (In this review container the fetch may be blocked — if so, you'll see the fallback tiles, which is the graceful behaviour.)
> 2. On the **right** of many items you'll see a **preview thumbnail** (a coloured stand-in for the page's preview image). Some items have **no preview** — those simply show no thumbnail, demonstrating "where available." Each preview is marked as a simulated stand-in.

Because these are the external-fetch parts, please react to **how the icon and preview sit in the layout and the "where available" behaviour**, not the exact pictures:

- Is showing the **real favicon with a clean fallback**, plus a **preview thumbnail only when one is available**, what you wanted?
- Is the **preview on the right at that size** the right placement and prominence, or would you prefer it larger/smaller or in a different spot?
- When **no preview exists**, is simply omitting it (as shown) fine, or would you want a neutral placeholder in its place?
